summary: The bill directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to coordinate with listed federal agencies to identify their biotechnology positions, assess current and 5- and 10-year future workforce needs including qualifications and security clearances, evaluate training and talent-exchange options, and report findings to Congress within 180 days.

This engages government spending by identifying potential future resource requirements, though it does not authorize or mandate new spending itself. The effect is therefore minor and leans toward possible expansion of spending.
